messages:
nina_engineer: Hey team, submitting an accommodation request — I'm getting severe respiratory irritation and dizziness from strong adhesive/solvent smell since building A had tile repairs this week. Doc recommends avoiding exposure to those fumes. I can go remote but need a short-term plan while the landlord remedies.

sam_manager: Thanks for flagging, @nina_engineer. Sorry you're dealing with that. Immediate options: 1) temporary remote until vendor clears the area; 2) move you to a different floor/wing if air isn't shared; 3) hoteling at our downtown satellite for a few days. Which do you prefer short-term?

nina_engineer: Remote for the next 48-72 hours would be best. If air tests still show VOCs, i can take a hotel for a few nights if company covers it.

liam_facilities: Opening Facilities ticket FCL-2026-9001: "Adhesive/solvent fumes — area assessment and HVAC test". We'll do immediate VOC air monitoring and contact the contractor about ventilation. ETA for on-site test: 4 hours.

casebot: HR case created: HR-2026-777 "Exposure sensitivity 1 adhesive fumes". Intake requested.

olivia_hr: @nina_engineer we received preliminary notice. Please complete the confidential intake form: https://hr.redwood.example/intake?case=HR-2026-777 or request a private call. HR can approve short-term remote and review any lodging stipend requests after intake. Medical documentation helps but we can start immediate temporary measures.

ben_legal: Quick legal note: document all accommodation offers and employee preference. Hoteling is an OK interim measure but check exec approval for offsite costs over policy thresholds. Also get details from the landlord/contractor about product MSDS and remediation timeline.

liam_facilities: Update: air monitor started, initial VOC spike near the repair zone (ppb above baseline). We've isolated the zone and increased fresh air flow. Requesting contractor to stop solvent use indoors and switch to low-VOC adhesive within 24 hours.

sam_manager: @nina_engineer reserving temporary remote and submitting equipment request if you need a hotspot or keyboard. Also requested a hoteling budget pre-approval from ops finance in case air stays unsafe.

nina_engineer: Thanks. Remote setup is fine for now; hotspot would help if wifi at home is flaky. Appreciate the hotel pre-approval in case it's needed.

olivia_hr: Next steps summarized: 1) Nina to complete intake or schedule confidential call; 2) Facilities to finish VOC testing and remediation plan (FCL-2026-9001); 3) Manager to arrange temporary remote and equipment; 4) HR drafts accommodation confirmation within 3 business days and coordinates any lodging approval if required. HR case HR-2026-777 logged.

liam_facilities: Contractor provided MSDS and agreed to cease solvent-based adhesives tonight. We'll ventilate for 24 hours and retest. If levels remain elevated we'll coordinate temporary relocation options for affected employees.

ben_legal: Also recommend tracking any symptoms reported by other employees in adjacent zones and include them in the case log. If landlord refuses mitigation we may need to escalate through Facilities/Real Estate.

sam_manager: I'll follow up with Nina via DM about equipment and keep team updated. Please post remediation timeline here when available.

nina_engineer: Appreciate everyone moving quickly. I'll fill the intake form this afternoon and ping @sam_manager about the hotspot. Please keep me posted on retest results.

liam_facilities: Will post retest numbers here within 36 hours. Ticket FCL-2026-9001 updated.

olivia_hr: Reminder: please DM any medical attachments rather than posting in channel. We'll close public thread when accommodation letter is signed in HR-2026-777.
